• First letter ⇒ Shifted to the fourth position.
 
• Second letter ⇒ Shifted to the third position

• Sixth and seventh letter ⇒ Interchanged their positions

Hence, "**RGESNET**" is the correct answer.

questions.question: In a code language, SAME is written as SMEA. How will FLOW be written in that language?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f3fce3500da2308a0da5bfbf6715215133a7f213e1088bf2bc3541913fedbd92.png] 

Logic: SAME is coded as SMEA by arranging the letters of the word 'SAME' in decreasing order of their numerical position in alphabetic order-

S → 19th position

A → 1st position

M → 13th position.

E → 5th position.

Decreasing order of 19, 1, 13, 4 is → 19, 13, 4, 1.

So, SAME is coded as- S(19) M(13) E(5) A(1)

By the same logic, FLOW will be coded as-

F → 6th position

L → 12th position

O → 15th position

W → 23rd position.

Decreasing order of 6, 12, 15, 23 is → 23, 15, 12, 6.

So, FLOW will be coded as W(23) O(15) L(12) F(6)

Hence, **FLOW should be written as WOLF**.

questions.question: In a certain code language, ‘ENVY' is coded as ‘FMWX' and 'ALAS' is coded as ‘BKBR’. What is the code for 'BODY' in the given code language?
questions.solution:
Here's the explanation presented in the requested format:

**Logic:**If a letter is in an odd position (e.g., first, third), it is shifted forward by one position in the alphabet.

If a letter is in an even position (e.g., second, fourth), it is shifted backward by one position in the alphabet.

'ENVY' is coded as ‘FMWX’,

E → F (+1)

N → M (-1)

V → W (+1)

Y → X (-1)

And 'ALAS' is coded as ‘BKBR’.

A → B (+1)

L → K (-1)

A → B (+1)

S → R (-1)

Similarly, 'BODY' will be coded by using the same logic.

B → C (+1)

O → N (-1)

D → E (+1)

Y → X (-1)

Hence, the correct answer is "**CNEX**".
